sourceStatus: No regime content. This dataset ships deliberately empty — see `note` and references/regimes.md.
note: The mechanism ships and the content does not. An obligation is the only thing this skill would state about what a regulator requires of the reader; everything else it says is about the reader's own register. A tool asserting an obligation it cannot cite to primary text is worse than one that stays quiet, because a reader cannot tell a checked claim from a plausible one and will act on both. `register_regime` refuses an obligation with no `source` and no `owningFunction`, so this cannot be quietly relaxed: whoever adds content has to have read the text, named the article, and decided who at the firm owns the duty.

roles.meaning: the organisation puts somebody else's AI system into use
the organisation develops or places an AI system on the market

roleNote: `aiRole` is the decisive gate. Much of what these regimes say is addressed to providers, and a firm that buys and deploys AI is usually a deployer. Conflating the two fills a register with obligations that are real and are somebody else's, and a reader cannot tell the difference because they read identically to the ones that apply.

shape.flag: the business-context profile key that selects it

obligations.requirement: what the text requires, in its own terms
obligations.owningFunction: who at the firm discharges it — required, and often not security
obligations.source: the article or section, and the date it was checked against primary text
obligations.securityWork: true when this is the security function's to do
